questions.question:
If the area of the region S=(x,y):2y-y2≤x2≤2y,x≥y is equal to n+2n+1-πn-1, then the natural number n is equal to  ________.

 

[JEE Main 2023, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The condition \(x^2\leq2y\) gives \(y\geq\dfrac{x^2}{2}\).

The condition \(x\geq y\) gives \(y\leq x\).

For the interval \(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\leq y\leq x\) to exist, we need \(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\leq x\).

Thus \(x(x-2)\leq0\), so \(0\leq x\leq2\).

The inequality \(2y-y^2\leq x^2\) can be written as \(x^2+y^2-2y\geq0\).

Completing the square, \(x^2+(y-1)^2\geq1\).

Therefore, the required points lie on or outside the circle \(x^2+(y-1)^2=1\).

For \(0\leq x\leq1\), the lower arc of the circle is \(y=1-\sqrt{1-x^2}\).

Within the strip \(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\leq y\leq x\), the part outside the circle is \(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\leq y\leq1-\sqrt{1-x^2}\).

For \(1\leq x\leq2\), we have \(x^2\geq1\), so \(x^2+(y-1)^2\geq1\) automatically.

Hence the total area is \(A=\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(1-\sqrt{1-x^2}-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)dx+\int_1^2\left(x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)dx\).

Since \(\displaystyle\int_0^1\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx\) is the area of a quarter circle of radius \(1\), its value is \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

Therefore, the first integral is \(1-\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{5}{6}-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

The second integral is \(\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}-\dfrac{x^3}{6}\right]_1^2\).

Thus the second integral is \(\left(2-\dfrac{8}{6}\right)-\left(\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{6}\right)=\dfrac{2}{3}-\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{1}{3}\).

Hence \(A=\dfrac{5}{6}-\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{7}{6}-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

Given \(A=\dfrac{n+2}{n+1}-\dfrac{\pi}{n-1}\), comparison of the coefficient of \(\pi\) gives \(n-1=4\).

Therefore, \(n=5\).

Also, \(\dfrac{n+2}{n+1}=\dfrac{7}{6}\) for \(n=5\), so the value is verified.

A circle passing through the point \(P(\alpha, \beta)\) in the first quadrant touches the two coordinate axes at the points \(A\) and \(B\). The point \(P\) is above the line \(A B\). The point \(Q\) on the line segment \(A B\) is the foot of perpendicular from \(P\) on \(A B\). If \(P Q\) is equal to \(11\) units, then the value of \(\alpha \beta\) is_______

 

[JEE Main 2023, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let the radius of the circle be \(r\).

As the circle touches both coordinate axes in the first quadrant, its centre is \((r,r)\).

The points of contact are

\(A=(r,0)\)

\(B=(0,r)\)

\(\therefore\) the equation of \(AB\) is

\(x+y=r\)

The point \(P(\alpha,\beta)\) is above \(AB\).

Its perpendicular distance from \(AB\) is

\(PQ=\dfrac{\alpha+\beta-r}{\sqrt{2}}=11\)

\(\alpha+\beta-r=11\sqrt{2}\)

As \(P\) lies on the circle,

\((\alpha-r)^2+(\beta-r)^2=r^2\)

\(\alpha^2+\beta^2-2r(\alpha+\beta)+r^2=0\)

Using \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta\),

\((\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta-2r(\alpha+\beta)+r^2=0\)

\(2\alpha\beta=(\alpha+\beta-r)^2\)

\(2\alpha\beta=(11\sqrt{2})^2=242\)

\(\alpha\beta=121\)

& =e^{(\ln \sec x+\ln x)} \\
& =x \sec x
\end{aligned}
\)

Solution is: \(y \cdot x \sec x=\int \frac{x \sec x}{x \cos x} d x\)

\(y \cdot x \sec x=\tan x+c\)

Since, \(y\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{\pi}\)

Hence, \(c=2 \sqrt{3}-\sqrt{3}=\sqrt{3}\)

\(x y=\frac{\tan x}{\sec x}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sec x} \)

\(x y=\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x \)

\(x y^{\prime \prime}+2 y^{\prime}=-\sin x-\sqrt{3}\cos x\)
Hence, \(\left|\frac{\pi}{6} y^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+2y^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right|=|-2|=2\)
